_note: How each person talks. Instructions for whoever or whatever writes a line, never shown to a player, so this file is English only and is not translated. Kept out of cast.*.json for exactly that reason. Plain notes on purpose: 'answers with numbers' is something a person or a model can both follow, where 'wry and world-weary' is not.

voices.maddox: Answers by pointing at somebody else. Gives you a name and a place. Never says what he thinks.
voices.tovin: Polite and tired. Says what the rule is, then says it is not fair, then applies it anyway.
voices.bell: Counts things. Gives a number in almost every answer.
voices.ossa: Gives instructions, not opinions. Short orders. Sit. Stand. Make noise.
voices.garrick: Talks in distances and days. A carter measures everything.
voices.wren: Prices everything. Says what a thing is worth and who buys it.
voices.bram: Says the plain thing and stops. Will talk about the fight and not about the village. Never asks why you want to learn.
voices.halgrave: Answers with figures. Proud of the works. Not ashamed of the dead and does not apologise.
voices.sena: Blunt and short. Under a dozen words when she can manage it. Angry but not dramatic.
voices.tom: Talks about before. Every answer has a then and a now in it. Never asks the player for anything until he has said why.
voices.ivo: A doctor. Precise and clinical. Knows his own excuse is poor and says so.
voices.cadan: States things. Does not explain himself and does not apologise for the land.
voices.nessa: Lists. Gives names and dates. Impatient with her father.
voices.pell: An old farmer. Repeats himself. Circles back to the same detail.
voices.ryse: Gives orders even when answering a question. No long sentences. No regret.
voices.odile: Everything is a transaction. Asks your price. Never denies anything.
voices.kell: Stops in the middle. Short pieces. Frightened but not weak.
voices.til: Says as little as possible. Often three words.
voices.mira: A lawyer. Gives cases and numbers. Angry and exact.
voices.corvin: A banker. Talks about money plainly. Not impressed by anyone.
voices.peyre: An archivist. Gives shelf numbers, dates and counts. Quiet.
voices.anselm: Qualifies everything. Says almost, about, I think. Never quite commits.
voices.hesper: Refuses. Short and final. Does not explain twice.
voices.aurel: Formal but plain. Admits the law is wrong and keeps signing it.
voices.arthur: Calm and certain. Corrects your facts before he answers. Never raises his voice and never apologises.
voices.dray: A soldier. Commands. Under fifteen words.
voices.guard: Bored. Says what he is paid to say and one thing he should not.
voices.watchman: Watches. States what he is there for.
voices.fairy: Oblique and very short. Often three or four words. Never explains, never argues, never names a person or a place she has no reason to know. She is dying and asking for help, and she does not dress it up.
